page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled with a 200 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mixed profile. The single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks placing it in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core performance scales down, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory performance is stable for large blocks, showing average read and write bandwidth, but exhibits weak performance for small-block cached reads.

The server exhibits notable bottlenecks in high-throughput and database workloads, with Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput both scoring in the poor category (bottom 10%). Similarly, Redis SET operations and Geekbench software compilation benchmarks are weak. Consequently, while the high memory capacity and strong single-core performance suit memory-intensive single-threaded tasks or lightweight caching, this instance is less optimal for heavy database operations, parallelized compilation, or high-throughput web serving.
